successCriteria.description: `findByQuery` honours `params.employeeIds`: when it is a non-empty array, the generated SQL includes a single `employee_id = ANY($n)` condition with the array pushed as one parameter value (not expanded into per-element placeholders), and the condition is placed before the LIMIT/OFFSET clauses.

`ILeaveService` and `LeaveService` expose `list(actor, query)` and `getById(actor, requestId)` returning `Promise<LeaveRequest>` / `Promise<LeaveRequest>` respectively, and `createLeaveService()` continues to satisfy `ILeaveService`.

`list` applies role scoping: EMPLOYEE → `employeeIds = [actor.id]`; MANAGER → `[actor.id, ...directReportIds]` where direct reports come from `employeeService.getEmployeesByManagerId(actor.id)` (one level only); ADMIN → no `employeeIds` filter. The scoped value is merged into the query and delegated to `repository.findByQuery`.

`getById` loads via `repository.findById`; when the request is null OR the actor may not see it under the same visibility rule as `list`, it throws `NotFoundError('Leave request not found')` — identical response for missing and non-visible requests.
Visibility is status-independent: a manager sees direct reports' requests in every status, and no status filter is introduced by the scoping logic.

constraints: Read-only operations: `list` and `getById` must never open a transaction or pass an optional client — call `repository.findByQuery` / `repository.findById` without the `client` argument.
No SQL in the service layer and no fetch-all-and-filter in application code: the `employeeIds` filter must be expressed as a repository WHERE condition, not post-filtered in the service.
No other repository changes beyond extending `findByQuery` to honour `employeeIds`.
No new shared type additions or constructor wiring changes: `employeeIds` already exists on `LeaveRequestQueryParams` and `employeeService` is already injected into `LeaveService`.
outOfScope: Sub-phase 6.3 — Tests for leave reads (leave.repository.test.ts, leave.service.test.ts, leave.routes.test.ts). No test files, test-existence, or coverage criteria are required by this sub-phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: The `LeaveRequest` shape is unchanged by this phase — no field is added, removed, or renamed; reads return the existing canonical contract.
`employeeIds` remains an optional `string[]`; an empty/undefined array means "no employee filter", a non-empty array restricts results to those employee ids.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Authenticated actor required; EMPLOYEE sees only own requests, MANAGER sees own + direct reports' requests, ADMIN sees all.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only; no transaction; returns LeaveRequest[] (possibly empty).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Authenticated actor required; same visibility rule as list — a caller who may not see the request receives the same NotFoundError as a non-existent request.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws NotFoundError('Leave request not found') for missing or non-visible requests; read-only, no transaction.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the existing `NotFoundError('Leave request not found')` message/type already thrown by the private `getRequest` helper and `repository.update`.
Reuse `LeaveRequestQueryParams` (including its existing `employeeIds?: string[]`) and `LeaveRequest` from the shared types without modification.

Match the existing `findByQuery` placeholder/`values` ordering convention (`$n` = `values.length`) so the new `employee_id = ANY($n)` condition composes correctly with existing status/date conditions and LIMIT/OFFSET.
Use `IEmployeeService.getEmployeesByManagerId(managerId)` for direct-report resolution (one level only), matching the existing manager-visibility semantics used elsewhere in the service.

integrationPoints.why: Resolves a manager's direct reports (one level) to build the MANAGER visibility scope for list/getById.
The service delegates all read data access to these repository methods; findByQuery must honour the merged employeeIds filter.
